ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: journeys planned ahead
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Choose who goes, where and when: the travellers get ready together, rested, fed, washed, packed and dressed for the road, and set off at the hour.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: A dawn departure leaves time for an early night. Plan it the afternoon before.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description:
A journey is an order of its own rather than a decree: it is for the few who go, at an hour you choose, and nobody else's mood or a decree's place is spent on it. Plan it from the Journeys section on the Decrees page or the World page, or from a town or place on the region map with "Plan a journey here".
The planner asks who goes (colonists, and the animals to bring), where to (a town or a place on the region map, or nowhere in particular for a length you choose) and when (an hour on a day, the next dawn at least ten hours off by default). It shows the days on the road by the game's own caravan estimate, the weather along the way and at the destination, what each traveller will change into, how their night before is shifted, and the packing list, which you can change line by line or add to from the stores. How long the food lasts against the road, and the load against the room, stay in sight at the foot of the planner.

li.heading: The day before and the last hours
li.text: A day before setting off, each traveller's timetable is shifted for the night before: to bed earlier or later so they wake rested 3 hours before the hour, without staying up so long they run themselves down, and an hour or more of recreation before that night when theirs would be low by then. In the last hours (4 by default, 2 to 8 in the settings) they put work aside and are left out of Rimfolk's gatherings; an emergency still calls them. One step at a time, when nothing more pressing calls them:

table.li: Change into clothes for the road | From the start of the last hours
Pick up their share of the packing list | From the start of the last hours
A meal, if under 80% fed | From 2.5 hours before
The bathroom and a wash, each when under 90% (with Dubs Bad Hygiene) | From 1.25 hours before
Wait at the gate | From 45 minutes before

li.after: Wounds are seen to first: someone with wounds to tend goes to bed and a doctor tends them, as the game does. The gate is the colony's caravan packing spot nearest the way out if it has one, else a few steps past the colony's last cell on the way from home to the edge of the map they leave by.

li.heading: What they take

points.li: Food for everyone's days on the road, a quarter more, and a spare day's worth: travel food first (packaged survival meals, then pemmican), then what keeps through the trip, the better and lighter first; food that would spoil on the way only when nothing else is left.
Medicine: half a dose each and one more for every 8 days on the road, the plainer kinds first, never more than half of the stores while anyone stays home.
A bedroll each for a trip of half a day or more, a double one counting for two, and any mod's tents found by name, one for every two travellers.
Feed for the animals (kibble, else hay) for the days the land gives no grazing, every day for those that don't graze.

li.after: Each traveller picks up their share of the food, medicine and bedding as they can carry it; the rest, the feed and anything else on the list is loaded at the gate by the game's own caravan forming, onto the pack animals first. What a traveller carries already counts toward the list and isn't loaded again.

li.heading: How long it lasts
li.text: At the foot of the planner, always in sight however far the window is scrolled:

points.li: Food for about so many days for the travellers, from their nourishment a day by the game's own hunger rates, against the days on the road (one way or there and back, as planned). Green when it covers the road with the margin (the road, a quarter more and a spare day), orange when it covers the road only, red when it falls short, with the shortfall in days and in meals of 0.9 nutrition, a simple meal's worth.
With animals, their feed against the days they can't graze, with the same margin; animals that graze all the way need none.
The weight still to take up against the room the travellers and pack animals have. A caravan carrying more than it can doesn't move.

li.after: The list is in groups (food, medicine, bedding, feed for the animals, other), each with its subtotal: days for food and feed, medicine a person, sleeping places for bedding, and the weight. Each line says whose number it is, the days it adds, its weight and how many are to hand, and warns of food that would spoil before the road ends; on hover, what the thing is, its nourishment and how long it keeps.

points.li: Type a number (kept to what is to hand), or step it with - and +: one at a time, 10 with Shift, 100 with Ctrl, as in the game's trade and caravan windows. All takes everything to hand, None sets it to none. A number you set is yours, shown in gold, and stays as you set it; the arrow beside it gives back the planner's.
The x takes one of the planner's lines off: the planner makes up its share from other things and leaves it off until you put it back or work the list out again.

Add from the stores lists everything the stores hold and the travellers carry, by kind (food, medicine, drugs, apparel, weapons, ammunition when a mod adds any, tools and gear, silver and trade goods, materials, everything) or by name, with how many there are and what one weighs. A click adds one, with Shift 10, with Ctrl 100; All adds everything there is. Food the travellers eat, medicine, bedrolls, tents and feed go in their groups; anything else goes under Other, with the caravan's goods.
Work the list out again gives back the planner's numbers and the lines you took off; the lines you added stay.

li.heading: Dressed for the road
li.text: The planner reads the land's own reckoning of every other hour of the trip, where they will be on the way (and back, for a trip there and back), and takes the coldest and the hottest with 3 degrees either way. A traveller who wouldn't be comfortable through that changes into clothes from the stores, a piece at a time while a piece brings them closer, the one worst off first and nobody's piece given twice. Armour, locked pieces and what you made them wear stay on. They keep those clothes on until they set off.

li.heading: Setting off
li.text: At the hour, if everyone is ready, the game's own caravan forming takes exactly the travellers, their animals and the rest of the goods, gathers at the gate and leaves by the edge of the map toward the destination; one of them says a word and those at home nearest the gate see them off. Their own timetables come back as they go.
li.after: If someone isn't ready (down, not in their right mind, wounds still to tend, under arms, away, at a ritual) or there is danger on the map, the others wait at the gate and a letter asks: wait an hour (the departure moves on an hour, and it asks again if need be), leave without them, or call the journey off. If whoever wasn't ready is ready before you answer, they set off as ordered. Called off, everyone's hours come back and the travellers put their packs back in the stores. One journey is planned at a time.
